newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends slightly down in consolidation.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends slightly down in consolidation.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures ended the day slightly lower as prices consolidated gains made on Wednesday, that carried the most-active December contract to 15-week highs, dealers said.
The benchmark contract closed 0.28 cent lower at 77.16 cents per lb, having ranged from 77.25 to 76.95 cents. The rest of the board settled 0.35 to 0.10 cent weaker.
A disappointing export and sales report, expectations for a cut in the U.S. Department of Agriculture's planted area estimate, and hot temperatures in the South may have contributed to losses.
But the move was blamed mostly on technical factors, analysts said, adding that prices should remain rangebound on Friday, ahead of Monday's key USDA report.
They said prices have absorbed a cut to about 14.0 million acres. A lower number could trigger speculative buying, while a less severe reduction would be bearish for prices, they said.
In March, the USDA pegged planted cotton area for the 1997/98 crop at 14.485 million acres.
Trade selling accounted for the bulk of the day's estimated volume of 18,000 lots, dealers said. The speculators were cited as the day's main buyers.
Firm technical resistance was pegged at 77.70 to 77.95 cents basis December.
Open interest in the July contract stood at 3,323 lots as of Monday, down 4,919 lots from the previous session.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture put new sales at 50,400 480-lb bales for upland cotton in the new crop, and at 15,100 bales for the current crop, for the week ended June 19.
Shipments of upland cotton reached 115,400 bales, in the current season.
Wednesday's official volume was 25,056 lots, NYCE said.
